text:
At t = 0, truck, starting from rest, moves in the positive x-direction at uniform acceleration of $5 ms^{-2}$. At t = 20 s, a ball is released from the top of the truck. The ball strikes the ground in 1 s after the release. The velocity of the ball, when it strikes the ground, will be :

(Given $g = 10 ms^{-2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


At t = 20 s,

velocity of truck,

v = 0 + 5 $\times$ 20 = 100 m/s

At 20 sec a ball is dropped from the truck, so velocity of ball will be same as truck.

Velocity of truck at x-direction = 100 m/s and in y-direction = 0.

$\therefore$ Velocity of ball $v_{x} = 100 m/s, v_{y} = 0$

Now ball will show projectile motion where vertically downward acceleration $g = 10 m/s^{2}$ acts on the ball.

As horizontally no acceleration acting on the ball so horizontal velocity 100 m/s will remain unchanged.

Velocity of the ball when it reach the ground along y-direction after 1 sec.

$v_{y}=0-10\times 1$

$\Rightarrow$ $v_{y}=-10$ m/s

$\therefore$ Velocity of ball $(\vec{v})=100\hat{i}-10\hat{j}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: If n main scale divisions coincide with (n + 1) vernier scale divisions. The least count of vernier callipers, when each centimetre on the main scale is divided into five equal parts, will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
5 parts of main scale division = 1 cm

$\therefore$ 1 part of main scale division = $\frac{1}{5}$ cm

$\therefore$ 1 M.S.D. = $\frac{1}{5}$ cm

(n + 1) vernier scale division = n main scale division.

$\therefore$ 1 V.S.D. = $\frac{n}{n+1}$ M.S.D.

= $\frac{n}{n+1}$ $\times$ 1 M.S.D.

= $\frac{n}{n+1}$ $\times$ $\frac{1}{5}$ cm

We know,

L.C. = 1 M.S.D. $-$ 1 V.S.D.

= $\frac{1}{5}$ cm $-$ $\frac{n}{5(n+1)}$ cm

= $\frac{n+1-n}{5(n+1)}$ cm

= $\frac{1}{5(n+1)}$ cm = $\frac{2}{n+1}$ mm
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: The radii of two planets A and B are in the ratio 2 : 3. Their densities are 3$ρ$ and 5$ρ$ respectively. The ratio of their acceleration due to gravity is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$\frac{r_{A}}{r_{B}}=\frac{2}{3}$

$\frac{ρ_{A}}{ρ_{B}}=\frac{3}{5}$

We know,

Acceleration due to gravity

$g=\frac{GM}{r^{2}}=\frac{G}{r^{2}}\times \frac{4}{3}πr^{3}\times ρ$

$=\frac{4πGrρ}{3}$

$\therefore$ $g\propto ρr$

$\therefore$ $\frac{g_{A}}{g_{B}}=\frac{ρ_{A}}{ρ_{B}}\times \frac{r_{A}}{r_{B}}$

$=\frac{3}{5}\times \frac{2}{3}$

$=\frac{2}{5}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: Two projectiles $P_{1}$ and $P_{2}$ thrown with speed in the ratio $\sqrt{3}$ : $\sqrt{2}$, attain the same height during their motion. If $P_{2}$ is thrown at an angle of 60${}^{\circ }$ with the horizontal, the angle of projection of $P_{1}$ with horizontal will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

Maximum height of a projectile $(H)=\frac{u^{2}\sin ^{2}θ}{2g}$

Given, Ratio of initial velocity of two projectile

$\frac{u_{1}}{u_{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}$

Both projectile reach the same maximum height.

$\therefore$ $H_{1}=H_{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{u_{1}^{2}\sin ^{2}θ_{1}}{2g}=\frac{u_{2}^{2}\sin ^{2}θ_{2}}{2g}$

$\Rightarrow u_{1}^{2}\sin ^{2}θ_{1}=u_{2}^{2}\sin ^{2}θ_{2}$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{u_{1}}{u_{2}}\right )^{2}=\left (\frac{\sin θ_{2}}{\sin θ_{1}}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \left (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}}\right )^{2}=\left (\frac{\sin 60^{\circ }}{\sin θ_{1}}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{3}{2}=\frac{3}{4\sin ^{2}θ_{1}}$

$\Rightarrow \sin ^{2}θ_{1}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow \sin θ_{1}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\sin 45^{\circ }$

$\Rightarrow θ_{1}=45^{\circ }$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: An air bubble of negligible weight having radius r rises steadily through a solution of density $σ$ at speed v. The coefficient of viscosity of the solution is given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Air bubble moves with constant speed v. So net force = 0.

$\therefore$ Buoyant Force = Viscous force

$\Rightarrow F_{b}=F_{v}$

$\Rightarrow σ\times \frac{4}{3}πr^{3}g=6πnrv$

$\Rightarrow n=\frac{2σr^{2}g}{9v}$

text: Two bodies A and B of masses 5 kg and 8 kg are moving such that the momentum of body B is twice that of the body A. The ratio of their kinetic energies will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

Mass of body A = 5 kg

Mass of body B = 8 kg

Momentum of body B is twice that of body A,

$\therefore$ $P_{B}=2P_{A}$

We know,

Kinetic Energy $(K)=\frac{P^{2}}{2m}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{K_{A}}{K_{B}}=\left (\frac{P_{A}}{P_{B}}\right )^{2}\times \frac{m_{B}}{m_{A}}$

$=\left (\frac{1}{2}\right )^{2}\times \frac{8}{5}$

$=\frac{1}{4}\times \frac{8}{5}$

$=\frac{2}{5}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: A coil of n number of turns wound tightly in the form of a spiral with inner and outer radii $r_{1}$ and $r_{2}$ respectively. When a current of strength I is passed through the coil, the magnetic field at its centre will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


In the width of $r_{2}-r_{1}$ total n turns presents.

$\therefore$ In 1 unit width $\frac{n}{r_{2}-r_{1}}$ turns presents.

$\therefore$ In the width of dr number of turns,

$n^{'}=\frac{n}{r_{2}-r_{1}}\times dr$

Magnetic field (dB) due to element of dr length is

$dB=\frac{μ_{0}\times I\times n^{'}}{2r}$

$=\frac{μ_{0}I}{2r}\times \frac{n}{(r_{2}-r_{1})}dr$

$\therefore$ Total magnetic field due to entire coil is,

$\int dB=\int\limits _{r_{1}}^{r_{2}}\frac{μ_{0}I}{2r}\times \frac{n}{(r_{2}-r_{1})}dr$

$\Rightarrow B=\frac{μ_{0}In}{2(r_{2}-r_{1})}\int\limits _{r_{1}}^{r_{2}}\frac{dr}{r}$

$=\frac{μ_{0}In}{2(r_{2}-r_{1})}\times [\log _{e}^{r}]_{r_{1}}^{r_{2}}$

$=\frac{μ_{0}In}{2(r_{2}-r_{1})}\times (\log _{e}^{r_{2}}-\log _{e}^{r_{1}})$

$=\frac{μ_{0}In}{2(r_{2}-r_{1})}\times \log _{e}\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: A sample of monoatomic gas is taken at initial pressure of 75 kPa. The volume of the gas is then compressed from $1200 cm^{3}$ to $150 cm^{3}$ adiabatically. In this process, the value of workdone on the gas will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For monoatomic gas degree of freedom f = 3 and $γ$ = $\frac{5}{3}$

Here for gas,

Initial pressure $(P_{1}) = 75$ kPa

Initial volume $(V_{1}) = 1200 cm^{3}$

Final volume $(V_{2}) = 150 cm^{3}$

Final pressure $(P_{2}) =$ ?

For adiabatic process,

$P_{1}V_{1}^{γ}=P_{2}V_{2}^{γ}$

$\Rightarrow 75\times (1200)^{γ}=P_{2}(150)^{γ}$

$\Rightarrow P_{2}=75\times \left (\frac{1200}{150}\right )^{\frac{5}{3}}$

$=75\times (8)^{\frac{5}{3}}$

$=75\times 32$ kPa

= 2400 kPa

Work done in adiabatic process,

$W=\frac{P_{2}V_{2}-P_{1}V_{1}}{1-γ}$

$=\frac{2400\times 10^{3}\times 150\times 10^{-6}-75\times 10^{3}\times 1200\times 10^{-6}}{1-\frac{5}{3}}$

$=\frac{(2400\times 150-75\times 1200)\times 10^{-3}}{-\frac{2}{3}}$

$=\frac{-810000\times 10^{-3}}{2}$

$=-405$ J
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: Which of the following equations correctly represents a travelling wave having wavelength $λ$ = 4.0 cm, frequency $ν$ = 100 Hz and travelling in positive x-axis direction?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, equation of wave travelling in positive x-direction is -

$y=A\sin (kx-wt)$

where $k=\frac{2π}{λ}$

and $w=2πf$

Here given $λ$ = 4 cm and frequency (f) = 100 Hz

$\therefore$ $k=\frac{2π}{4}=0.5π$ $cm^{-1}$

and $w=2π\times 100=200π$ $s^{-1}$

$\therefore$ Equation of travelling wave,

$y=A\sin (0.5πx-200πt)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text:
An expression for oscillating electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given as $E_{z} = 300 \sin (5π$ $\times$ $10^{3}x$ $-$ 3$π$ $\times$ $10^{11}t) Vm^{-1}$

Then, the value of magnetic field amplitude will be :

(Given : speed of light in Vacuum c = 3 $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{-1})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given the electric field expression:

$E_{z}=300\sin (5π\times 10^{3}x-3π\times 10^{11}t)\text{Vm}^{-1}$

The amplitude of the electric field ($E_{0}$) is $300\text{V/m}$.

The velocity ($v$) of the wave in the medium is given by the ratio of the coefficients of time and displacement in the wave equation, which can be calculated as:

$v=\frac{\text{Coefficient of}t}{\text{Coefficient of}x}=\frac{3π\times 10^{11}}{5π\times 10^{3}}=\frac{3}{5}\times 10^{8}\text{m/s}$

The relationship between the electric field amplitude and the magnetic field amplitude in an electromagnetic wave is given by:

$B_{0}=\frac{E_{0}}{v}$

Substituting the values for $E_{0}$ and $v$ into this formula:

$B_{0}=\frac{300}{\frac{3}{5}\times 10^{8}}$

$B_{0}=\frac{300\times 5}{3\times 10^{8}}$

$B_{0}=\frac{1500}{3\times 10^{8}}$

$B_{0}=5\times 10^{-6}\text{T}$

Therefore, the amplitude of the magnetic field ($B_{0}$) is $5\times 10^{-6}$ T.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: An electric cable of copper has just one wire of radius 9 mm. Its resistance is 14 $\Omega$. If this single copper wire of the cable is replaced by seven identical well insulated copper wires each of radius 3 mm connected in parallel, then the new resistance of the combination will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initially, copper wire radius $(r_{1}) = 9 mm$

Resistance (R) = 14 $\Omega$

We know, $R=\frac{ρL}{A}=\frac{ρL}{πr_{1}^{2}}=14$

Now this copper wire is replaced by 7 parallel copper wire of resistance $R_{1}$.

$\therefore$ Equivalent resistance of 7 parallel copper wire,

$\frac{1}{R_{eq}}=\frac{1}{R_{1}}+\frac{1}{R_{1}}+\frac{1}{R_{1}}+\frac{1}{R_{1}}+\frac{1}{R_{1}}+\frac{1}{R_{1}}+\frac{1}{R_{1}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{R_{eq}}=\frac{7}{R_{1}}$

$\Rightarrow R_{eq}=\frac{R_{1}}{7}$

$=\frac{1}{7}\times \frac{ρL}{πr_{2}^{2}}$

$=\frac{1}{7}\times \frac{ρL}{π\left (\frac{r1}{3}\right )^{2}}$ [as $r_{2}=\frac{r_{1}}{3}$ ; $r_{1}=9$ mm and $r_{2}=3$ mm]

$=\frac{1}{7}\times \frac{ρL}{πr_{1}^{2}}\times 9$

$=\frac{1}{7}\times 14\times 9$

$=18\qquad \Omega$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: Find the ratio of maximum intensity to the minimum intensity in the interference pattern if the widths of the two slits in Young's experiment are in the ratio of 9 : 16. (Assuming intensity of light is directly proportional to the width of slits)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let,

Width of first slit $= w_{1}$ and width of second slit $= w_{2}$

Given, $\frac{w_{1}}{w_{2}}=\frac{9}{16}$

Given,

Intensity of light $(I)\propto w$

$\therefore$ $\frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}=\frac{w_{1}}{w_{2}}=\frac{9}{16}$

We know,

$\frac{I_{\max }}{I_{\min }}=\left (\frac{\sqrt{I_{1}}+\sqrt{I_{2}}}{\sqrt{I_{1}}-\sqrt{I_{2}}}\right )^{2}$

$=\left (\frac{\sqrt{\frac{I1}{I2}}+1}{\sqrt{\frac{I1}{I2}}-1}\right )^{2}$

$=\left (\frac{\frac{3}{4}+1}{\frac{3}{4}-1}\right )^{2}$

$=\left (\frac{7}{1}\right )^{2}$

$=\frac{49}{1}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: Eight similar drops of mercury are maintained at 12 V each. All these spherical drops combine into a single big drop. The potential energy of bigger drop will be $____________ E$. Where E is the potential energy of a single smaller drop.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From law of conservation of charge

$\begin{array}{l} q_{i}=\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{f}}\Rightarrow 8\times (4π\mathrm{E}_{0}\mathrm{R})\times 12=\left (4πER^{1}\right )\times \mathrm{V}_{f} \\  \\ \Rightarrow 96\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{f}}\mathrm{R}^{1} \\  \\ \text{And,}8\times \dfrac{4}{3}πR^{3}=\dfrac{4}{3}πR^{1}3 \\  \\ 8=\left (\dfrac{R^{1}}{R}\right )^{3} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{R}^{1}=2\mathrm{R} \end{array}$

From (i) & (ii), we get

So, $96\mathrm{R}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{f}}\times 2\mathrm{R}\Rightarrow \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{f}}=48$ Volt

$\begin{array}{l} V_{f}=\dfrac{1}{2}C_{f}V_{f}^{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\times \left (4πε_{0}\mathrm{R}^{1}\right )\mathrm{V}_{f}^{2} \\  \\ =\dfrac{1}{2}\times (4πε_{0}\times 2\mathrm{R})\times 48^{2} \\  \\ =\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\times 4πε_{0}R\times 12^{2}\right )\times \dfrac{48^{2}\times 2}{12^{2}}=32E \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text: The refractive index of an equilateral prism is $\sqrt{2}$. The angle of emergence under minimum deviation position of prism, in degree, is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Refractive index

$\begin{array}{l} μ=\dfrac{\sin \left (\frac{A+δ\min }{2}\right )}{\sin \left (\frac{A}{2}\right )}\Rightarrow \sqrt{2}=\dfrac{\sin \left (\frac{60+δ\min }{2}\right )}{\sin 30^{\circ }} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\sin \left (\dfrac{60+δ\min }{2}\right )\Rightarrow 45^{\circ }=\dfrac{60+δ\min }{2} \\  \\ \Rightarrow δ\min =30^{\circ } \\  \\ δ=\mathrm{i}+\mathrm{e}-\mathrm{A} \\  \\ \text{Here,}e=i \\  \\ \text{So,}δ\min =2\mathrm{e}-\mathrm{A}\Rightarrow 2\mathrm{e}=δ\min +\mathrm{A} \\  \\ e=\dfrac{δ\min +A}{2}=\dfrac{30^{\circ }+60^{\circ }}{2}=45^{\circ } \end{array}$

text: A hydrogen atom in its first excited state absorbs a photon of energy x $\times$ $10^{-2} eV$ and excited to a higher energy state where the potential energy of electron is $-$1.08 eV. The value of x is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a Bohr orbit the total energy of the electron is half its potential energy, $E=\dfrac{U}{2}$.

Final state: $E_{f}=\dfrac{-1.08}{2}=-0.54\text{eV}$.

First excited state ($n=2$): $E_{i}=-\dfrac{13.6}{2^{2}}=-3.4\text{eV}$.

Energy of the absorbed photon:

$\Delta E=E_{f}-E_{i}=-0.54-(-3.4)=2.86\text{eV}=286\times 10^{-2}\text{eV}$

Hence, the answer is 286.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift

text:
The circuit diagram used to study the characteristic curve of a zener diode is connected to variable power supply (0 $-$ 15 V) as shown in figure. A zener diode with maximum potential $V_{z} = 10 V$ and maximum power dissipation of 0.4 W is connected across a potential divider arrangement. The value of resistance $R_{P}$ connected in series with the zener diode to protect it from the damage is $________________$ $\Omega$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th June Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Power $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{zm}}=\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{zm}}\mathrm{V}_{z}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{ZM}}=\dfrac{P_{zM}}{V_{z}}=\dfrac{0.4}{10}=0.04\mathrm{A} \\  \\ \text{So,}R_{P}=\dfrac{E_{\max }-V_{z}}{I_{ZM}}=\dfrac{15-10}{0.04}=\dfrac{5}{0.04}=125\Omega  \end{array}$
